subject: On-call scale qualification & warm-pool playbook
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@finlytics.io>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: On-call scale qualification & warm-pool playbook

Jane — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the load test:

Summary of what we heard from Finlytics:
- Primary workload: conversational streaming (token-by-token) used in client-facing chat across web and mobile.
- Target steady concurrency: 800 active chat sessions during peak.
- Burst pattern: 2x baseline for ~10–18 minutes during batch releases.
- Acceptable SLOs (customer stated): p95 streaming tail latency < 450 ms; request-level success > 99.5%.

Redwood proposal for qualification and acceptance criteria (draft):
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 450ms for streaming token latency under target concurrency.
- Throughput/concurrency: sustain 800 active sessions with 300–350 QPS aggregate.
- Scale-up: cold-to-ready (new instance available to serve streaming) target <= 60s for fast path, fallback allowance up to 90s with graceful queueing.
- Warm pool: initial warm-pool sizing to cover ~20% of target concurrency (recommended starting point = 160 warm sessions) with rapid top-up autoscaling.
- Queueing behavior: soft-queue with max wait target p95 < 15s, enqueue cap 200 requests.

Next actions (proposed):
1) We will run an internal preflight load test on 2028-04-14 (UTC) — please confirm availability for that window.
2) Finlytics to share a small traffic sample and one representative conversation set (anonymized) for us to replay.
3) We will provide a test-run playbook + acceptance checklist by EOD tomorrow (attached: proposed_loadtest_plan.pdf, slo_acceptance_criteria.md).
4) Redwood will attach a temporary test API key and a short post-test summary with raw metrics and traces.

Attachments (stubs):
- proposed_loadtest_plan.pdf (PDF, ~6 pages)
- slo_acceptance_criteria.md (Markdown)

If that aligns with you, confirm and we will lock the 14 Apr test window and hand off technical ownership to Markus for the execution and measurements.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Grace — thanks for the clear summary and for proposing concrete numbers. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Concurrency: 800 active sessions is correct for peak. We also see short spikes to ~1,100 for ~5–7 minutes during marketing pushes.
- Streaming latency SLO: p95 < 450ms is what product requires; we'd like to validate p99 behavior as well (p99 target < 1.2s).
- Cold starts: we can tolerate up to 90s for the first connection during a major release event, but prefer to keep normal cold-starts below 60s.
- Warm pool: 160 warm connections ok to start; we'll iterate if tests show different priming needs.

I've attached a 60-minute sample of anonymized traffic and a couple of sample conversations for replay. Also attaching our procurement lead contact in case we need faster turnaround on contract/PO.

Attachments (stubs):
- finlytics_prod_traffic_sample.json (application/json)

We are available for the 2028-04-14 test window you proposed — please send preflight checklist and role/credential details for the test account. Also, our security team asked for the SOC2 report link prior to execution: can you share that?

Regards,

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@finlytics.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Apr 2028 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-call scale qualification & warm-pool playbook

Jane — thanks for the prompt turnaround and the sample traffic. A couple of technical notes and the measurement approach we will use for the run: 

Warm-pool sizing and scale-up mechanics (proposal):
- Initial warm-pool formula: warm_pool_size = ceil(target_concurrency * 0.2) + safety_buffer(2). For 800 target => 162 (round up to 165 for distribution across zones).
- Instance readiness: for our m-7b-quantized profile the fast-path spin/attach time we can target ~25–40s; worst-case cold bootstrap (model load + KV priming) measured up to 90s.
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive ramp for first 60s (scale to target 70% within 30s), then linear fill to full capacity over next 90s to avoid overshoot.

Queueing and fallback behavior:
- Soft-queue design: requests beyond warm pool are queued with FIFO aging; we will configure a max queue time threshold of 30s with enforced retry hints to the client. Acceptance criterion for test: p95 queue-wait < 15s with <1% queue-drop.

Measurement & acceptance plan for the 14 Apr run:
1) Baseline run: replay sample at 1x peak (800) and record latency histograms and dropped requests.
2) Burst run: 2x burst (~1,600) for 10 minutes to verify warm-pool + autoscaling behavior.
3) Stress window: short 1k–1.2k sustained step to measure steady-state tail latencies and queue behavior.
4) Streaming token-level tracing: enable token-level traces for a 5% sample to inspect tail causes.

Attachments to our run: jmeter_fintlytics_chat_plan.jmx (load scenario), and a preflight checklist we will post to the shared drive. We will capture CloudTrace and per-route cost/time breakdowns and share a consolidated CSV.

Posting link to artifacts and checklist: https://redwood-internal.share/drive/rdw-2028-0234/load-tests

I will own execution; Grace will coordinate results and SRE notes. Laura — can you slot the run into our CI bench for 14 Apr (morning window PST)?

—Markus
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
